weeks.title: Q2:W3 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to model the associative property as a strategy to multiply.
sc: I can use pictures to solve the associative property of multiplication problems.
I can solve expressions using associative property.

days.lo: I am learning to apply the distributive property and the fact 9 = 10 – 1 as a strategy to multiply.
sc: I can determine the units and number of units in a multiplication expression.
I can represent units and the number of units using strip diagrams.
I can use the distributive property and a 10 fact with subtraction to solve a 9 fact.

days.lo: I am learning to interpret the unknown in multiplication and division to model and solve problems.
sc: I can model multi-step word problems using strip diagrams and label the unknown quantities.
I can write multiplication and division equations using a question mark or box for the unknown.
I can solve multi-step word problems by finding the unknown values in order.

days.lo: I am learning to reason about and explain arithmetic patterns using units of 0 and 1 as they relate to multiplication and division to solve the unknown.
sc: I can multiply and divide using units of 1 to find the unknown.
I can multiply and divide using units of 0 to find the unknown.

weeks.title: Q2:W4 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to solve two-step word problems involving all four operations and assess the reasonableness of solutions with a model.
sc: I can use the Read, Draw, Write (RDW) process to model and break down two-step word problems.
I can write and solve equations representing both steps of a word problem.

days.lo: I am learning to represent multiply by multiples of 10 by using the place value chart and arrays.
sc: I can represent multiplying single-digit numbers by tens using place value disks on a chart.
I can explain how multiplying by a multiple of 10 shifts digits one place value to the left.
I can write multiplication equations in unit form (e.g., 2 x 3 tens = 6 tens and standard form (2 x 30 = 60).

days.lo: I am learning to use place value strategies and the associative property n × (m × 10) = (n × m) × 10 (where n and m are less than 10) to multiply by multiples of 10.
sc: I can use a chart to find an equation.
I can use parentheses in the equations to find the related fact.

days.lo: I am learning to use strategies and to represent two-digit by one-digit multiplication with concrete objects.
sc: I can represent expressions with place value disks and place value chart.
I can record the partial products vertically.

weeks.title: Q2:W5 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I will multiply two-digit numbers by one-digit numbers using strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm.
sc: I can represent two-digit by one-digit multiplication using place value disks or partial products.
I can use the standard algorithm to record regrouping and calculate the final product.
I can explain how partial products relate to the standard multiplication algorithm.

days.lo: I will use strategies and algorithms, including the distributive property, to multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number.
sc: I can use a ruler to measure the length of the sides.
I can find the area of a rectangle.

days.lo: I am learning to understand area as a two-dimensional surface attribute that can be covered by tiling with non-overlapping shape units without gaps.
sc: I can completely cover a 2D surface using pattern block units without leaving gaps or overlapping shapes.
I can trace or draw unit boundaries to show how pattern blocks tile a shape.
I can count and record the total number of pattern block units required to cover a shape.

days.lo: I am learning to measure and compare the area of rectangles by tiling with standard square units (square inches and square centimeters) and decomposing shapes to form rectangular arrays.
sc: I can estimate how to draw the missing square units inside an array.
I can draw rows and columns to determine the area.

days.lo: I am learning to relate the side lengths of a rectangle to the number of tiles along its sides to distinguish between side length and total area.
sc: I can explore the relationship between units and area.
I can relate area to multiplication to draw rectangular arrays.
I can tile a rectangle completely using square inch or square centimeter unit tiles without gaps or overlaps.

weeks.title: Q2:W6 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to find the area of a rectangle through multiplication of the side lengths.
sc: I can arrange unit square tiles into arrays without gaps or overlaps to form rectangles.
I can label the side lengths (number of rows and columns) of my tiled rectangle.
I can use area and side length to find unknown side length.

days.lo: I am learning to apply the distributive property as a strategy to find the total area of a larger rectangle by adding two products.
sc: I can use centimeter tiles to find the area of rectangle.
I can write the expression to represent a tiled area.

days.lo: I am learning to solve word problems to determine an area.
sc: I can solve area word problems with 1 side length unknown.
I can choose a strategy to find the area of a larger rectangle.

days.lo: I am learning to find the area of composite shapes by decomposing into rectangles.
sc: I can use the break apart and add strategy to find the area of a composite shape.
days.note: two further SC bullets (subtracting to find area) are struck through in the IPC and omitted

weeks.title: Q2:W7 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to find areas by decomposing into rectangles or completing composite figures to form rectangles.
sc: I can choose an appropriate method for finding the area of a composite shape.
I can solve a word problem involving the area of non-rectangular shapes.

days.lo: I am learning how to partition a whole into equal parts, identifying and counting unit fractions using concrete models.
sc: I can partition fraction strips into equal parts.
I can partition a whole amount of liquid into equal parts.
I can count unit fractional parts of a whole.

days.lo: I am learning how to partition a whole into equal parts, identifying and counting unit fractions by folding fraction strips.
sc: I can fold fraction strips into equal parts.
I can name and label unit fractional parts of a whole.

weeks.title: Q2:W8 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to recognize that equal parts of an identical rectangle can havedifferent shapes.
sc: I can divide a shape into equal parts in more than one way.
I can prove halves are equal with different shapes.
I can create multiple shapes using equal squares.

days.lo: I am learning how to partition a whole into equal parts and define the equal parts to identify the unit fraction numerically.
sc: I can divide a shape or model into a specified number of equal parts.
I can name each unit or part.
I can explain that the bottom number (denominator) represents the total number of equal parts in a whole and the top number (numerator) represents one part.

days.lo: I am learning how to build non-unit fractions less than one whole from unit fractions.
sc: I can use fraction form to draw a shape partitioned into equal parts.
I can represent a unit fraction with shading.
I can represent non-unit fractions pictorially.

weeks.title: Q2:W9 Math IPC Grade 3 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to identify and represent shaded and non-shaded parts of onewhole as fractions.
sc: I can identify the shaded fractional part of a whole.
I can identify the empty/unshaded fractional part of a whole.

days.lo: I will compare two unit fractions by reasoning about their sizes and justifying conclusions using symbols, words, objects, and pictorial models.
sc: I can use fraction strips and pictorial models to compare two unit fractions with different denominators.
I can explain that as the denominator increases, the size of each fractional unit decreases when comparing the same whole.
I can write a correct comparison sentence using the <, >, or = symbols.

days.lo: I will compare two unit fractions by reasoning about their sizes and justifying conclusions using symbols, words, objects, and pictorial models.
sc: I can use fraction strips and pictorial models to compare two unit fractions with different denominators.
I can explain that as the denominator increases, the size of each fractional unit decreases when comparing the same whole.
I can write a correct comparison sentence using the <, >, or = symbols.
days.note: Flex Day (lessons combined, same cell as Tue)

days.lo: I will represent fractions greater than zero and less than or equal to one with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 using number lines.
sc: I can partition a number line between 0 and 1 into equal fractional parts.
I can locate and label unit and non-unit fractions on a number line.
I can use a number bond or fraction strip to prove my fraction placement on the number line.

days.lo: I will represent fractions greater than zero and less than or equal to one with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 using number lines.
sc: I can partition a number line between 0 and 1 into equal fractional parts.
I can locate and label unit and non-unit fractions on a number line.
I can use a number bond or fraction strip to prove my fraction placement on the number line.
